description: Closed SSOT for Champollion translation-domain codes. The 17 content codes below are the ONLY domains a corpus card may declare for dev.domain / test.domain / pairGeneration.domain. The classifier (arena/scripts/corpora-builder/corpora_builder/domain_classifier.py VALID_DOMAINS) and the corpora-card schema (cli/shared/schemas/corpora-card.schema.json) both reference this list — keep all three in sync. This taxonomy is what unblocks the per-pair 'general' score (pool a pair's domain corpora, score once, pie-chart the composition) and domain-specific routing.

domains.ui: User-interface strings — buttons, menus, settings, dialogs, notifications, app chrome.
domains.legal: Legal and judicial text — contracts, statutes, court proceedings, clauses, compliance.
domains.medical: Clinical and healthcare text — diagnoses, treatments, prescriptions, patient care.
domains.financial: Banking, accounting, and investment text — transactions, balances, audits, markets.
domains.edu: Educational material — lessons, textbooks, curricula, classroom and academic learning content.
domains.ecommerce: Online-retail text — products, carts, orders, shipping, returns, customer reviews.
domains.marketing: Promotional and brand text — campaigns, slogans, advertising and persuasion copy.
domains.gov: Government and public-administration text — policy, legislation, civic services, enforcement.
domains.scientific: Research and academic science — hypotheses, methods, results, abstracts, papers.
domains.religious: Religious and devotional text — scripture, prayer, worship, ritual. LABEL ONLY (see notes.religious).
domains.support: Customer/technical support text — troubleshooting, help, tickets, FAQs, escalations.
domains.subtitles: Film/TV subtitles and spoken dialogue — short lines, stage directions, transcribed speech.
domains.news: Journalism and reporting — articles, press releases, current events, citizen journalism.
domains.literary: Literary prose and poetry — novels, verse, narrative fiction, descriptive prose.
domains.conv: Everyday conversational text — casual dialogue, social posts, general-purpose sentences.
domains.tech: Software and engineering text — APIs, servers, protocols, configuration, infrastructure.
domains.humanitarian: Crisis-response and humanitarian text — public-health, disaster, and aid information (e.g. TICO-19, Gamayun / CLEAR Global).

mixed.definition: No single dominant content domain — the corpus spans several. 'mixed' is a COMPOSITION MARKER, not a content domain, and is NEVER itself a coverage credit. A domain of 'mixed' MUST be accompanied by a domainDistribution that breaks the corpus down into the content codes above; 'mixed' as a bare label (no distribution) is not permitted.

notes.religious: 'religious' stays in the vocabulary for honest LABELING only and is NEVER a coverage credit. Bible / religious sources are excluded from scoring elsewhere (colonial-data doctrine), so labelling a corpus 'religious' documents what it is without ever earning it ranking eligibility.
notes.humanitarian: Added beyond the 16 keyword-classifiable codes. It is assigned as a deliberate card fact (TICO-19, Gamayun), never auto-classified — the keyword classifier has no 'humanitarian' keywords, so it only ever appears when an author labels it.
notes.mixed-vs-content: Exactly the 17 content codes are valid as a sole/primary domain. 'mixed' is the one allowed non-content value and only with a domainDistribution. Anything else hard-fails the registry build (arena/scripts/build_registry.py).
